top_story: US airstrikes on Iranian targets on 1 September mark a clear escalation from the exchange of fire the previous weekend, sharply raising the risk that a contained confrontation will harden into a broader regional conflict. This military shift lands in a region where Gaza’s supposed post-ceasefire reconstruction remains inseparable from bombardment and externally imposed control, leaving civilians trapped between physical ruin and political management of aid and recovery. The death of Israeli chemist Ada Yonath carries national symbolic weight but does not alter the strategic picture now defined by widening coercive action and shrinking political space. The emerging regional pattern is one in which conflict management is displacing conflict resolution, deepening insecurity from state-to-state confrontation to everyday civilian survival.
